title.narrative: Aguatuya – decentraliserade modeller för vattenrening i Bolivia

description.narrative:
Programmet syftar till att utveckla och främja ekonomiskt och ekologiskt effektiva decentraliserade sanitetsmodeller för urbana och peri urbana områden med 2000- 10 000 invånare. Insatsen fokuserar på uppförandet av vattenreningsverk som tillåter: -att sluta vattencykeln och ta vara på näringsämnen -replikering av dessa modeller inom olika ekologiska sammanhang geografiska och ekonomiska kontexter -en uppskalning av modellerna på nationell nivå
De viktigaste resultaten som programmet skall uppnå under hela programstödet är; -återanvändning av vatten och avfallshantering (näringsämnen) -en förbättring av institutionella förhållanden hos lokala organisationer som ger sanitetsservice -implementering av hållbar sanitetsservice på projektplatser/anläggningar -utveckling av normer och riktlinjer på nationell nivå -utveckling av finansiell service som kan bidra till en uppskalning av dessa modeller
Den nationella organisationen Agua Tuya är föreslagen som ambassadens avtalspart och huvudpart i implementeringen av programmet. Agua Tuya kommer att arbeta i främst sex områden: Cliza, Tolata, Tarija, Santiago de Huata och Montero för att uppnå ovan nämnda resultat. För utveckling av finansiella tjänster som kan bidra till ekonomisk hållbarhet och uppskalning av sanitetsmodellerna kommer Agua Tuya att arbeta med en nationell finansieringsinstitution.

The aim of the program is to promote decentralized ecological and economically efficient sanitation models (in urban areas and cities between 2,000 and 10,000 inhabitants) with a focus on waste water plants that will allow: i) the closing of the water cycle ii) the replication of those models in different ecological contexts iii) the scaling up of the models at national level
The main results that the program must achieve during the whole contribution are: - the reuse of water and solid waste (as nutrients) - the enhancing of institutional conditions in local organizations that provide sanitation services - the implementation of sustainable sanitation services in project sites (Cliza, Punata, Tolata, Tarija, Santiago de Huata, Montero) - the development of norms and guidelines at the national level - the development of financial services that can contribute to the scaling up of these models

The aim of the program is to promote decentralized ecological and economically efficient sanitation models (in urban areas and cities between 2,000 and 10,000 inhabitants) with a focus on wastewater plants that will allow:
i) Closing the water cycle and achieve nutrient recovery
ii) Enabling conditions for the development of local institutions and organizations providing sanitation services
iii) Scaling-up of the sustainable sanitation management models.

The overarching achievements of the first phase are highlighted below, which has been reached through the program applying the decentralized sanitation approach:
- Strategic sanitation planning model with a single vision among key actors on the different sanitation solutions to be implemented in the future within a municipal territory; implemented in Tarija and Cliza municipalities.
- Demonstrating at full scale the potential of decentralized wastewater management, as a competitive alternative or complement to centralized wastewater management. Cliza municipality now treats 100% of the wastewater produced by the city and its communities. To achieve this objective, three WWTPs were implemented with funding from Sweden, and another 3 WWTPs with funds leveraged from Swiss Development Cooperation, together with important local counterpart from the municipality of Cliza. The treated wastewater from the 6 WWTPs is reused for agricultural irrigation during the dry season.
- Providing examples of different management models of WWTPs that ensure the operation and sustainability over time, considering all necessary components of a functional system, e.g., technical, financial, environmental, and institutional sustainability.
- Adapting different existing technologies for the treatment of wastewater and sludge to the Bolivian context, in the three ecological zones of Bolivia, i.e., highlands, valleys and lowlands. The program has implemented a variety of wastewater treatment technologies, innovative sludge-management systems for on-site system (e.g. septic tanks), and urine management (e.g. through an adsorption technology adapted from Swedish innovation company).
- The implementation of wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) with social acceptance, which function as reference models at the national level, showing the importance and benefits of social participation. The participation of key actors, such as municipal authorities, leaders of local associations and communities, representatives of the civic committee, companies, and water committees, throughout the project cycle which has contributed to the sustainability of the project (and good governance). As well as, increased involvement of the population in the care for the environment and the proper management and reuse of treated wastewater.
- That farmers and irrigators recognize the potential of the approach of reusing treated wastewater for irrigation and nutrient recovery for crops, improving the productivity of their cropland. The WWTPs plants have generated a great demand for the treated wastewater within the agricultural communities around the treatment plants, who compete for this additional water resource, which is available throughout the year.
